title: DRAGGING GOD'S NAME INTO A LIE

memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "He went to his father and said, 'My father.' 'Yes, my son,' he answered. 'Who is it?' Jacob said to his father, 'I am Esau your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may give me your blessing.' Isaac asked his son, 'How did you find it so quickly, my son?' 'The LORD your God gave me success,' he replied" - Gen 27:18-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The lies now come thick and fast. "I am Esau your firstborn" — a bold, direct falsehood. But the most troubling words are these: "The LORD your God gave me success." Jacob drags God's holy name into his deception, using the Lord as the excuse for his quick "hunting." To cover one lie, he pins it on God.

This is a serious thing. It is one matter to sin; it is another to use God's name to make the sin sound spiritual. We can do this too — claiming "God led me" to justify a decision we made for selfish reasons, or wrapping our own agenda in religious language. Using God's name to cover our schemes is a misuse of that name.

The commandment not to take the Lord's name in vain is not only about careless swearing; it is about attaching God's name to things that are not of Him. When we say "God told me" to win an argument or excuse a wrong, we take His name lightly.

Let us be careful and reverent with the name of God. It should never be a tool to make our deceptions sound holy. Instead, let His name be honoured by lips that speak truth.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Have you ever used "God's leading" to justify what you wanted anyway?
Do you treat God's name with reverence in how you speak?
Where do you need to be more honest rather than cloaking things in spiritual language?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for any time I have used Your name to cover my own wishes. Help me to honour Your name and to speak the truth plainly. Amen.
